```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../setup.R")
docs_setup()
```

A complex function of a complex variable maps a plane to a plane, which needs four real dimensions to graph. Colour can carry two of them, and a surface over the plane or the sphere carries the rest. Knots and immersed surfaces are curves and surfaces whose shape in space is the subject. This article draws each with a dedicated stat. Installation is covered in [Get started](ggplot3d.html), and [Surfaces, solids and fields](surfaces-solids.html) covers parametric surfaces in general.

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
```

## Domain colouring on the Riemann sphere

Domain colouring paints each point $z$ with the phase of $f(z)$ as hue (Wegert [2010](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2295)). Zeros are the points where all hues meet in counter-clockwise order, and poles are where they meet in the opposite order. On the Riemann sphere, the complex plane closed by a point at infinity, the behaviour at infinity is visible too. $f(z) = (z - 1)/(z^2 + 1)$ has one zero at 1 and poles at $\pm i$.

```{r riemann-sphere, fig.alt = "A sphere painted by the phase of a rational function, with colours circling one zero and two poles."}
ggplot() +
  stat_riemann_sphere_3d(fun = function(z) (z - 1) / (z^2 + 1), n = 32) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster"), axes = character(),
           panes = character(), box = "none")
```

The raster backend keeps the many small faces of the colouring from producing a large vector file.

## Riemann surfaces

An inverse function such as $\sqrt[3]{w}$ has several values at each point. Its Riemann surface stacks one sheet per value and joins them so the function is single-valued on the surface (Poelke and Polthier [2009](https://diglib.eg.org/handle/10.1111/v28i3pp0735-0742)). `stat_riemann_surface_3d()` takes the forward function, here $w = z^3$, and the number of sheets.

```{r riemann-surface, fig.alt = "The three-sheeted Riemann surface of the cube root, spiralling three times around its branch point."}
ggplot() +
  stat_riemann_surface_3d(fun_inverse = function(w) w^3, sheets = 3, n = 24,
                          fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  coord_3d()
```

## Möbius transformations

A Möbius transformation $f(z) = (az + b)/(cz + d)$ maps circles to circles on the Riemann sphere. `mobius_3d()` returns the map as a function that accepts complex numbers, points on the sphere or points in the upper half-space. The inversion $f(z) = 1/z$ swaps 0 and infinity and fixes 1.

```{r mobius}
f <- mobius_3d(a = 0, b = 1, c = 1, d = 0)
f(c(0, 1, Inf))
f(rbind(c(0, 0, 1), c(0, 0, -1)), model = "sphere")
```

On the sphere the same map swaps the north and south poles.

## Torus knots

A $(p, q)$ torus knot winds $p$ times around the axis of a torus and $q$ times through its hole; it is a knot when $p$ and $q$ share no factor. `stat_knot_3d()` draws it as a tube. The $(2, 3)$ torus knot is the trefoil.

```{r knot, fig.alt = "A trefoil knot drawn as a tube winding twice around and three times through a torus."}
ggplot() +
  stat_knot_3d(p = 2, q = 3, radius = 0.12, n = 120, sides = 10, fill = "#B5342B") +
  coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

[Gallery](gallery.html#parametric-curves) builds the same trefoil from a data frame with `geom_tube_3d()`.

## Immersed surfaces

The Klein bottle and Boy's surface cannot be built in three-dimensional space without passing through themselves. `stat_immersed_3d()` draws standard immersions of such surfaces: `"klein_figure8"`, `"klein_bottle"`, `"boy"`, `"cross_cap"` and the Möbius strip `"moebius"`.

```{r klein, fig.alt = "The figure-eight immersion of the Klein bottle, a tube with a figure-eight cross-section that passes through itself."}
klein <- ggplot() +
  stat_immersed_3d(type = "klein_figure8", n = c(32, 20), fill = "#2A7A7A") +
  coord_3d()
klein
```

The scene resolves each crossing exactly, so the faces in front cover the ones behind on both sides of the self-intersection. [Meshes and intrinsic geometry](meshes.html#where-a-mesh-crosses-itself) draws the crossing curve itself with `stat_self_intersection_3d()`.

## References

Wegert, E. (2010). Phase plots of complex functions: a journey in illustration. <https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2295>
